titulo: One canonical only: www or non-www
lead: To you, yoursite.com and www.yoursite.com are the same site. To a search engine, they can be two. When the canonical, the sitemap, and the links disagree, Google picks on its own which address to keep, and sometimes it picks the wrong one. This lesson closes that door.
objetivo: choose www or non-www and make canonical, sitemap, JSON-LD, and links use the same address.

aprende.t: What a canonical is and why it decides which URL counts
Redirect the variations to a single one
Check the 4 places where the address appears
The real case of the non-www canonical

hero_alt: Two blank street signs in front of a house; a man on a ladder is working on one of them.

secoes.titulo: From the address you type to the address that counts

nos.detalhe: The same content can answer at http://, https://seusite.com and https://www.seusite.com. With no rule, that's three addresses competing.
Pick one version and make the others redirect to it permanently (301 or 308). The X-ray in lesson 2 shows this in the Redirects block.

The link rel="canonical" tag tells the search engine which address is the official one for that page. It must point to the version you chose, with https and with (or without) www, the same across the whole site.
Canonical, sitemap, JSON-LD and internal links all use the same address. One mismatched canonical in one part of the site is enough for Google to pick a different URL.

secoes.legenda: It doesn't matter whether you use www or not. What matters is making one choice and using it everywhere.

texto: See which version Search Console already shows most, and which one outside links use. Stick with that one.
Changing later is costly: choose once and write it down.
The redirect rule lives at your host, on the server, or on the CDN. Ask your provider for a permanent redirect from the version that doesn't count to the one that does.
Check with the X-ray: all three variations should end at the same address with 200.
In the X-ray, the canonical line for each page should show the address you chose. Empty or different is a finding.
Watch out for parts of the site generated by another system (blog, knowledge base, store): that's where the canonical tends to differ.
Open the sitemap and see whether the URLs use the same version. Do the same in the JSON-LD and in the menu and footer links.
If part of the HTML is generated by a script, fix it in the generator, or the fix disappears on the next build.

exemplo.texto: The canonical for /conhecimento/ was missing www, while the portal's sitemap used www. The fix went into the repository and the generator, with a note so no one undoes it.

secoes.sub: The same commands the X-ray uses, one at a time.

blocos.conteudo:
for u in http://www.seusite.com/ https://seusite.com/ https://www.seusite.com/; do
  echo "$u -> $(curl -4 -m 20 -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' "$u")"
done

abas.rot: What it looks like when it's right
abas.html:
Redirects for www.inema.club in the 10/19/2026 X-ray:

http://www.inema.club/ -> 308 https://www.inema.club/
https://inema.club/ -> 308 https://www.inema.club/
https://www.inema.club/ -> 200

Both variations redirect permanently to the www version, which answers 200.

• A temporary redirect (302) instead of a permanent one.
  • Canonical pointing to the home page on every page: the search engine understands that only the home page counts.
  • Fixing the generated HTML instead of the generator: the error comes back on the next build.

secoes.sub: Use the raio-x.txt from lesson 2 as your starting point.

exercicios.texto: Run the curl loop (or the X-ray again) and see where each variation of the address goes.
exercicios.pronto: all three variations end at the same address, with a 200 at the end; if not, the fix request was made to your hosting.

exercicios.texto: Fill in the table of the 4 places for the home page and for one inner page.
exercicios.pronto: the table is complete and every row says "yes," or every "no" has its fix noted.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: What is the right choice: with www or without www?
opcoes: Either one, as long as it is the same one everywhere.
perguntas.explica: The search engine does not prefer one version. The problem is having two: canonical, sitemap, JSON-LD, and links need to agree.

perguntas.p: INEMA's /conhecimento/ had a canonical without www and a sitemap with www. The risk was:
opcoes: Google choosing another URL as the official one.
perguntas.explica: Conflicting signals leave the decision to Google. One divergent canonical in a single subsystem is enough for it to pick another URL.

perguntas.p: The page is generated by a script. Where do you fix the canonical?
perguntas.explica: If you fix only the HTML, the next build undoes it. In INEMA's case, the generator was fixed and got a warning.

perguntas.p: Which redirect code should you use between the variations?
perguntas.explica: A permanent redirect says the old address is no longer valid. A 200 on both versions is exactly what duplicate content is.

itens.texto: With or without www, either is fine; two, never.
canonical, sitemap, JSON-LD, and links, all the same.
Generated HTML is fixed at the source, not in the published file.
